cards.name: Fixed gameplay update
cards.summary: Gameplay logic advances once every third video retrace, giving 20 updates per second on the 60 Hz version, and each stored speed moves an actor 1.5 times its value per update.
cards.behavior: The game state sets the update rate to 3. The scheduler waits that many video retraces before it swaps the frame buffer. On a 60 Hz display the world, actors, camera, and player therefore advance 20 times per second, which is 50 ms per update. On the 50 Hz PAL N64 build the same rate gives about 16.7 updates per second, so many table values are 1.2 times larger there. The pause menu setup lowers the rate to 2 and a tile transition lowers it to 1. The actor position step multiplies every stored velocity by the rate times 0.5, so at rate 3 a stored speed of 6.0 moves the actor 9.0 world units per update, or 180 units per second. Accelerations, deceleration steps, timers and fixed offsets are not scaled. Link animations advance by playback speed times the rate times 0.5 frames per update, which is 1.5 animation frames per update at normal speed.

constants.name: fieldsPerUpdate
constants.unit: video retraces (fields) per gameplay update at 60 Hz, giving 20 gameplay updates per second

constants.name: positionStepRateFactor
constants.unit: multiplier on the update rate in the actor position step, so rate 3 gives 1.5x each stored velocity per gameplay update at 20 Hz

constants.name: animationStepRateFactor
constants.unit: multiplier on the update rate in the Link animation step, so rate 3 gives 1.5 animation frames per update at playback speed 1.0

constants.name: pauseUpdateRate
constants.unit: video retraces per gameplay update while the pause menu opens (30 Hz)

constants.name: tileTransitionUpdateRate
constants.unit: video retraces per gameplay update during a tile transition (60 Hz)

cards.name: Ground movement speed
cards.summary: The control stick maps to a target speed, then clamps to a boot-specific run cap after slope and water penalties.
cards.behavior: Stick magnitude produces a target speed. Linear mode scales the magnitude by 0.8. Curved mode removes a deadzone of 20 stick units, applies a cosine-square ramp scaled by 30 and offset by 7, then scales the result by 0.14. A slope term subtracts 8 times the square of the floor-pitch sine, with the sine capped at 0.6. The final target is clamped between zero and the current speed cap. The boot table sets the cap in hundredths of a speed unit: 600 for adult Link in normal boots, 550 for child Link, 550 for hover boots, 300 for iron boots on land, and 500 in any indoor room. Speed moves toward zero by 8.0 per update. Stored speeds are velocity units, so a cap of 6.0 moves the actor 9.0 world units per update. Walking toward a wall within about 69 degrees of head-on scales the cap by the angle times 0.00008, down to a floor of 0.1. Deep water halves several movement speeds through a water speed factor of 0.5.

constants.unit: hundredths of a velocity unit per gameplay update at 20 Hz, adult Link in normal boots (child 550, hover 550, iron on land 300, indoors 500); position advances 1.5x this per update

cards.name: Forward roll
cards.summary: A forward roll scales walking speed by 1.5, keeps a minimum speed, and can bonk at high speed.
cards.behavior: In the Z-target action handler, an action-button press with the stick forward or neutral starts a roll. The handler does nothing in an indoor room, on the slippery floor type, or on a floor with a blocking floor effect. With a melee weapon held, Link starts a jump slash instead. Roll target speed is 1.5 times the normal walk target, with a floor of 3.0 speed units. The roll animation plays at 1.25 times normal rate on the 60 Hz version and 1.5 on PAL, halved in water. At 20 Hz it advances about 1.9 animation frames per update. Invulnerability starts at animation frame 8, around the fourth update, and lasts 10 updates on the 60 Hz version. From frame 15 an action can interrupt the roll, and at frame 20, around the eleventh update, the roll ends. At a speed of 7.0 or more, a wall within 45 degrees of straight ahead reverses the roll and starts the bonk response.

constants.name: rollSpeedMultiplier
constants.unit: multiplier over normal walk target speed, applied per gameplay update at 20 Hz

constants.name: rollMinSpeed
constants.unit: velocity units per gameplay update at 20 Hz (position advances 1.5x this per update)

constants.unit: velocity units per gameplay update at 20 Hz (position advances 1.5x this per update)

constants.unit: animation frames from the roll start (about 1.9 frames pass per gameplay update at 20 Hz)

constants.name: invulnerabilityDuration
constants.unit: gameplay updates at 20 Hz, stored as a negative invulnerability timer that counts up to zero (PAL uses -8)

constants.name: animationRate

cards.name: Jump and fall
cards.summary: Link has no free jump button. A ledge run-off launches an automatic jump from a speed-based vertical velocity, while boot-table gravity of -1.0 per update and a fall-speed clamp shape the arc.
cards.behavior: The boot table stores gravity of -100 hundredths, so vertical velocity drops 1.0 per update. Iron boots on land use -160 and iron boots underwater use -40. Falling speed clamps at -20 on the 60 Hz version and -24 on PAL. These are velocity units, so the position moves 1.5 times the velocity each update. Running off a ledge starts an automatic jump when the ground was just left, the floor is more than 20 units below, the speed is above 3.0, the heading is within 45 degrees of the body and no sword swing is active. The launch vertical velocity is 1.25 plus 0.2 times the current speed for adult Link. The speed factor is 0.4 for child Link. Above 5.9 for adult Link or 5.4 for child Link, the launch is a flat 7.5. The boot table also stores a 6.0 jump value, which only a Link actor outside the player category uses for a Z-target hop. Iron boots underwater lower it to 4.0. The airborne state ends when a floor check reports ground contact.

cards.name: Swimming and buoyancy
cards.summary: Water halves movement speed and uses a custom buoyancy model with separate rise and sink clamps.
cards.behavior: Entering deep water sets a water flag and halves the movement speed factor. Underwater vertical motion ignores normal gravity. When the body is less deep than an age threshold, the model applies a downward acceleration of 0.1 plus half of any upward velocity, with a sink clamp. Deeper than that, it applies an upward acceleration of 0.1 plus 0.3 times the current fall speed, with a rise clamp. These are velocity units per update, and position advances 1.5 times the velocity. Rise is clamped at 2.0 and sink at 5.0 on the 60 Hz version. Iron boots apply a downward 0.2 while the fall speed is slower than 3.0. Water deeper than 100 units marks the deep-water state. In the dive action, releasing the dive button makes the ascent target a vertical velocity of 0.018 times the stored water depth plus 4.0, capped at 8.0.

constants.name: waterSpeedFactor
constants.unit: movement-speed multiplier, applied per gameplay update at 20 Hz

constants.name: riseClamp
constants.unit: velocity units per gameplay update at 20 Hz (PAL uses 2.4; position advances 1.5x this per update)

constants.name: sinkClamp
constants.unit: velocity units per gameplay update at 20 Hz (negative means downward; PAL uses -6.0; position advances 1.5x this per update)

constants.name: surfaceDamping

cards.name: Ledge hop, step-up and climb
cards.summary: Ledge height picks a hop, a step-up or a hanging pull-up, and the thresholds differ by age. Vine walls and push blocks use separate height tests.
cards.behavior: A wall touch casts a probe down from above the head. Ledges lower than 18 units are ignored. A ledge below the step-up minimum, 41 for adult Link and 27 for child Link, selects a hop after 3 updates of pushing: the launch is 0.08 times the ledge height plus 5.5 and the forward speed is 2.5. Higher ledges select a step-up climb. Up to 59 (adult) or 39 (child) uses the short step-up. From there to 79.4 (adult) or 47 (child) uses the taller step-up, and Link is moved to the ledge top while the animation hides the offset. At or above 79.4 (adult) or 47 (child), Link starts a hanging pull-up. The step-up starts after 6 updates of pushing, or at once on a button press. If the wall surface carries flag 6 and belongs to a moving collision body, it needs both the 6 updates and a press. The climb animation plays at 1.3 times normal rate. A wall at least 79 high with climbable surface flags starts a wall climb instead. A wall surface with flag 6 that is at least 39 high, touched on the ground, lets Link grab a block while the action button is held.

cards.name: Player collision probe
cards.summary: Wall radius and ceiling height change with age, the wall probe height is the same for both ages, and a deep floor drop clears the grounded state.
cards.behavior: Each gameplay update checks walls, floor, and ceiling around the player. Both ages use a wall check height of 26 world units. Adult Link uses a wall radius of 18 and a ceiling check of 56. Child Link uses a radius of 14 and a ceiling check of 40. Crawling shrinks the wall radius to 10, wall height to 15, and ceiling check to 30. The floor probe starts 50 units above the feet and snaps the player to a floor at or above the feet. A floor more than 11 units below the player clears the ground flag and starts the leaving-ground state. Ceiling contact zeroes upward velocity.

cards.name: Normal follow camera
cards.summary: The default camera follows at a distance factor between 200 and 300 with a 60 degree field of view.
cards.behavior: The normal camera loads a distance minimum of 200 and maximum of 300 from its mode data. These are hundredths of player height, which is 68 world units for adult Link, so the distances are about 136 and 204 units. The height offset factor is -20, the pitch target is 10 degrees, and the field of view is 60 degrees. The field-of-view rate settles to 0.05 of the remaining error each camera update. The camera pitch is clamped between 14500 (about 79.7 degrees) and -15500 (about -85.2 degrees) in binary angle units. Background geometry can pull the camera inward. When health is 16 units or less, which is one heart, the field of view target is scaled by 0.8 for a tighter low-health view.

cards.name: Jump camera
cards.summary: The airborne camera uses its own distance factors, yaw rate, and a soft vertical eye follow.
cards.behavior: When Link is in the jump state, the camera switches to its jump mode. A plain fall uses a separate free-fall mode, and wall climbs use their own mode. The jump mode uses distance factors from 200 to 300 and a height offset factor of -20, in hundredths of player height. The yaw update divisor target is 12. The yaw-follow response uses a curve parameter of 0.35. Pitch stays between -9100 (about -50 degrees) and 14500 (about 79.7 degrees) in binary angle units. The eye position follows the target vertically at 0.2 of the remaining error per update. The result is a looser, higher view during jumps.

cards.name: Z-targeting lock-on
cards.summary: The Z button locks a focus actor, holds attention priority 40, and switches hostile targets to the battle camera.
cards.behavior: A fresh lock sets a 15-update timer and stores the focus actor. While Z stays held, or a switch lock is on, the timer counts down to 5 and stays at 5, so the reticle remains active. While the timer is 6 or more, which is about 10 updates after a new lock, the leash distance is ignored so the reticle can settle. A timer below 5 means the lock has ended. The focus actor receives attention priority 40 each update. A hostile focus selects the battle camera, which aims for an eye distance of 180 world units, unscaled by player height, and a field of view of 50 degrees. That field of view is scaled by 0.8 while a melee weapon is active or health is 16 or less. The distance ratio also shrinks the field of view by up to 0.05 of its value. A friendly focus uses the keep-on camera instead. Z held with no target uses the parallel camera.

cards.name: Sword combo
cards.summary: Sword swings share an 8-update combo window, and every third repeated swing advances to a finisher.
cards.behavior: Each sword swing sets a countdown of 8 updates. The swing counter resets when that countdown ends. A new swing of the same kind inside the window raises the counter. When the counter reaches 3, the swing index moves up by 2, which selects the finisher variant. A forward-stick stab sets a flag. On animation frame zero of the next swing action, that flag gives a forward lunge of 15.0 speed units, except for the hammer. The speed then decays by 5.0 per update. Damage flags depend on the held weapon: Master Sword, Kokiri Sword, Biggoron Sword, Deku Stick, or hammer. A jump slash uses separate flags.

constants.name: comboWindow
constants.unit: gameplay updates at 20 Hz, countdown that keeps the swing counter alive

constants.name: repeatedSwingLimit
constants.unit: swing count, checked per swing at 20 Hz gameplay updates

constants.name: finisherAnimationOffset
constants.unit: swing animation index steps added once, when a swing starts

constants.name: forwardLungeSpeed
constants.unit: velocity units per gameplay update at 20 Hz (position advances 1.5x this per update)

constants.name: attackSpeedDecay
constants.unit: speed units removed per gameplay update at 20 Hz (not scaled by the 1.5x position factor)

cards.name: Charged spin attack
cards.summary: Holding attack charges a spin in 0.02 steps. Release at 0.85 or more gives the strong spin, and a release before 0.1 cancels the charge.
cards.behavior: Holding the attack button starts the spin charge action and slows Link to a stop through the normal deceleration. Charge rises 0.02 per update from 0 toward 1.0, which is 50 updates, or 2.5 seconds, at 20 Hz. Releasing at 0.85 or above performs the strong spin. A quick stick rotation also gives the strong spin. Releasing between 0.1 and 0.85 gives the smaller spin. Releasing before the charge reaches 0.1 cancels it and plays the sheathing motion without a swing. The rotation check needs four stick samples above a magnitude of 55. Each sample is an angle in 2.8-degree steps, doubled for the test. Each sample must differ from the next by at least 10 in a consistent direction. A spin sets 8 updates of invulnerability.

constants.name: chargeStep
constants.unit: charge fraction per gameplay update at 20 Hz

constants.name: fullChargeThreshold
constants.unit: charge fraction, checked per gameplay update at 20 Hz

constants.name: minimumReleaseCharge
constants.unit: charge fraction, below this the release cancels the charge, checked per gameplay update at 20 Hz

constants.name: invulnerabilityDuration
constants.unit: gameplay updates at 20 Hz, stored as a negative invulnerability timer that counts up to zero

constants.name: stickRotationStep
constants.unit: doubled stick-angle samples (each raw step is 0x200 binary angle units, about 2.8 degrees), minimum change between neighbors, tested per gameplay update at 20 Hz

cards.name: Damage reaction and invincibility
cards.summary: Light hits flinch, heavy ground hits slide Link back at 23 speed units, and a hit grants 20 updates of intangibility.
cards.behavior: A damaging hit first checks the invincibility timer. A nonzero timer blocks health loss. For a normal grounded reaction, damage below 5 produces a light flinch and a small rumble. Damage of 5 or more adds a backward slide at a speed of 23.0 and selects a heavier hit animation. A knockback or airborne hit instead passes a forward speed of 4.0 and an upward speed of 5.0 to the knockdown. Every hit call sets 20 updates of intangibility, which blocks both damage and the damage response. Frozen and electrified responses replace the standard animation and rumble. The shared actor damage helper clamps health at zero. It applies to enemies, because Link health uses a separate change function.

constants.unit: health points (16 equals one heart), checked on the damage update at 20 Hz

constants.name: knockdownSlideSpeed
constants.unit: velocity units per gameplay update at 20 Hz for the heavy grounded hit slide (position advances 1.5x this per update)

constants.name: hitIntangibility

constants.name: knockbackUpwardSpeed

cards.name: Arrow and seed flight
cards.summary: Arrows fly at 150 units per update with a 12-update life, while seeds fly at 80 with a 15-update life.
cards.behavior: A fired arrow sets a projectile speed of 150.0 and a timer of 12 updates. A seed or nut sets 80.0 and 15 updates. These speeds are velocity units, so at 20 Hz an arrow moves 225 world units per update and a seed moves 120. The flight step moves the projectile, checks walls, and shapes the arrow to its velocity. Arrows that stick in the world remain for 20 updates. Lit and elemental arrows remain for 60. Once the flight timer falls below 7.2 updates, the arrow receives a downward acceleration of 0.4 per update. Elemental arrows keep their own damage flags.

constants.unit: velocity units per gameplay update at 20 Hz (position advances 1.5x this per update)

constants.unit: velocity units per gameplay update at 20 Hz (position advances 1.5x this per update)

cards.name: Hookshot travel and pull
cards.summary: The hookshot flies at 20 units per update, uses a 13 or 26 update reach limit, and pulls with speed tiers.
cards.behavior: A fired hookshot sets a projectile speed of 20.0, which is 30 world units per update at 20 Hz. The hookshot reach timer is 13 updates and the longshot uses 26. A hit on a hookable target attaches the chain and ends the reach timer. After the timer ends, the retract step moves the chain tip toward the body by a fixed distance per update: 30 when the chain pulls the player toward a hooked object, 50 when it pulls a hooked actor toward the player, and 200 when it retracts free. The pull toward an object sets the player velocity to a magnitude of 30. The hook detaches from a moving actor when the relative offset grows beyond 50 world units. When the chain snaps back to the player, vertical velocity drops by 20.

constants.unit: velocity units per gameplay update at 20 Hz (position advances 1.5x this per update)

constants.unit: gameplay updates at 20 Hz

constants.name: freeRetractSpeed
constants.unit: world units the chain tip moves toward the body per gameplay update at 20 Hz when it retracts free (direct step, not scaled by 1.5x)

constants.name: returnVerticalVelocityChange
constants.unit: velocity units per gameplay update at 20 Hz subtracted from player vertical velocity on the return snap

cards.name: Boomerang flight
cards.summary: The boomerang flies at 12 units per update, homes toward a focus for 20 updates, then returns.
cards.behavior: A thrown boomerang sets a projectile speed of 12.0, which is 18 world units per update at 20 Hz. It starts with a return timer of 20 updates. While a target exists, the flight steers toward it by closing a fraction of the heading error each update. The fraction is the shortfall from 200 world units times 0.005, with a floor of 0.12. After the return timer expires, the boomerang targets the player and can be caught within 40 world units. A wall hit reverses its heading and starts the return early. The boomerang can carry a small collectible back to the player.

constants.name: flightSpeed
constants.unit: velocity units per gameplay update at 20 Hz (position advances 1.5x this per update)

constants.name: returnTimer
constants.unit: gameplay updates at 20 Hz

constants.name: steeringScale
constants.unit: heading-error fraction per world unit of distance deficit, applied per gameplay update at 20 Hz

constants.name: minimumSteering
constants.unit: heading-error fraction closed per gameplay update at 20 Hz

constants.name: catchDistance
constants.unit: world units, checked per gameplay update at 20 Hz

cards.name: Bomb fuse and blast
cards.summary: A lit bomb waits 70 updates, flashes on a 7-update cycle, then grows a blast collider by 8 units per update.
cards.behavior: A spawned bomb starts with a fuse of 70 gameplay updates, which is 3.5 seconds at 20 Hz. Its flash interval scale starts at 7 and halves when the timer reaches 40, 20 and 3. The bomb falls under an acceleration of -1.2 per update and bounces with reduced speed. At detonation the explosion collider uses a scale of 100 percent and a model radius of zero. Its world radius grows by 8 units per update plus any variant offset, for 10 updates. The explosion damages actors through the attack collider, starts a camera quake, and requests a distance-scaled controller rumble.

constants.name: fuseUpdates
constants.unit: gameplay updates at 20 Hz (3.5 seconds)

constants.name: flashInterval
constants.unit: flash interval scale at fuse start, halved at timers 40, 20 and 3, per gameplay update at 20 Hz

constants.name: gravity
constants.unit: velocity units per gameplay update squared at 20 Hz (negative means downward)

constants.name: colliderScale
constants.unit: percent of the model sphere radius (100 percent equals scale 1.0)

constants.name: blastGrowth
constants.unit: world units of blast radius added per gameplay update at 20 Hz (not scaled by 1.5x), for 10 updates

constants.name: blastDuration
constants.unit: gameplay updates at 20 Hz during which the explosion collider grows
